0.long_answer: Follicular lymphoma is the disease that is characterized by small cleaved cells, the translocation t(14;18), and overexpression of the anti-apoptotic protein Bcl-2. This translocation places the BCL2 gene under the influence of the immunoglobulin heavy chain promoter, leading to its overexpression, which in turn prevents apoptosis and contributes to the survival of the malignant cells. The presence of small cleaved cells (centrocytes) is a hallmark of this indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and the genetic alteration is found in approximately 90% of cases, making it a defining feature of follicular lymphoma.
